checkOutcomes.evidence: The site is hard-coded to one dark palette and does not react to the user color-scheme preference.
The reduced-motion probe found no running animations and no auto-advancing content under `reduce`.
The forced-colors screenshot remains operable, but axe found four serious contrast failures and CSS has no prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptation.
Navigation and content swaps are abrupt; the CSS probe found no View Transition declarations.
No parallax, scrollytelling, entry reveal, or other scroll-linked animation exists on the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, entry reveal, or other scroll-linked animation exists on the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No swipe, pull, carousel, draggable, or other gesture-driven control exists on the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No swipe, pull, carousel, draggable, or other gesture-driven control exists on the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The long 6,200px listing keeps static chrome and provides no scroll progress or position-aware navigation.
No user-facing tooltip or popover requiring anchored positioning was found.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-facing tooltip or popover requiring anchored positioning was found.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Breadcrumbs on detail pages and the explicit “Search Results for” heading make destination and context clear.
No full-screen interstitial obscured content on load; the domain notice is compact and dismissible.
The page ships a custom `.modal`/WordPress editor overlay and no dialog, popover, or details primitives.
On mobile, logo, search, menu, eight category pills, and a domain banner consume roughly the first half viewport before content.
Home, listing, search, and detail layout captures at 360x800 reported zero horizontal overflow and include a viewport meta tag.
Components resize at the viewport level, but CSS inspection found no container queries for reusable cards/navigation.
Programmatic keyboard focus showed `outline: none`; many controls are 34–43px high, below a 44px touch target.
The listing immediately exposes search, categories, poster cards, and descriptive download titles.
The primary download journey diverts through multiple identical generic links to `linksmod.top`, rather than exposing a clear predictable file action.
A real HTTP 404 returns a visible “Error 404 Not Found” state with search-based recovery.
Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8s and FCP 3.0s, outside the good loading range; CLS 0.042 and TBT 0ms were good.
Observed CLS was 0.00022 on home and 0.0206 on detail, both comfortably low.
The trace reported zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; one 64ms detail-page task was isolated.
The load transferred 2.23MB across 83 requests; four parser-inserted head scripts lack async/defer and the HAR found multiple blocking candidates.
The public page ships WordPress admin editor, TinyMCE, media-upload, jQuery UI, and link-editor bundles unrelated to viewing movie listings.
axe found a critical unnamed search button and a serious unnamed back-to-top link; search input also has no explicit label.
axe measured ratios as low as 2.37:1 for search text and 3.03:1 for Telegram text, below 4.5:1.
axe found no main landmark and non-unique navigation landmarks; focus probing found no visible outline.
Detail body copy renders low-contrast gray on charcoal with dense line breaks and inconsistent emphasis, reducing reading comfort.
Narrow reflow works, but many category and navigation controls are only 34–43px high; the embedded trailer has no local text equivalent.
Lighthouse captured a TypeError in `width.js` reading `clientWidth` from null.
All 24 images use legacy PNG/JPEG without srcset; 23 are oversized and the logo lacks dimensions.
Public pages expose WordPress editor/link UI, load dated editor/plugin bundles, and create an iframe with an invalid `https://undefined/…` origin.
Home has descriptive title and meta description; detail has a unique descriptive title and article metadata.
Links use real hrefs, viewport metadata is present, and robots permits normal search crawling.
Pages return successful status, expose canonical URLs, allow indexing, and a current 22-part sitemap index is available.
Home exposes CollectionPage/Open Graph metadata and the detail page exposes matching Article JSON-LD.
HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy headers are all absent.
The page contacted 15 third-party origins including analytics and opaque ad-like domains; 79/83 HAR requests were classified third-party from the original host.
No geolocation/notification/media permission request or authentication surface was found, so no out-of-context prompt or password-only flow was imposed.
No HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP/Trusted Types baseline is configured.
Raw HTML contains 100% of rendered content tokens and crawler screenshots retain the complete listing without JavaScript.
Runtime robustness is undermined by a null `clientWidth` exception and a malformed `https://undefined/…` iframe on the detail template.
This is a server-rendered content/download catalog, not an app-like experience; no install/offline intent is evident.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a server-rendered content/download catalog, not an app-like experience; no install/offline intent is evident.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No scheduled events, times, recurring intervals, or time-zone-sensitive user data were found.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scheduled events, times, recurring intervals, or time-zone-sensitive user data were found.

findings.summary: The site is hard-coded to one dark palette and does not react to the user color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The site is hard-coded to one dark palette and does not react to the user color-scheme preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `color-scheme: light dark` and preference-driven surface/text tokens.

findings.summary: The forced-colors screenshot remains operable, but axe found four serious contrast failures and CSS has no prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptation.
findings.evidence: The forced-colors screenshot remains operable, but axe found four serious contrast failures and CSS has no prefers-contrast/forced-colors adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add high-contrast tokens and forced-colors fallbacks, then meet WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: Navigation and content swaps are abrupt
findings.evidence: Navigation and content swaps are abrupt; the CSS probe found no View Transition declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long 6,200px listing keeps static chrome and provides no scroll progress or position-aware navigation.
findings.evidence: The long 6,200px listing keeps static chrome and provides no scroll progress or position-aware navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll progress/position affordance for long result listings.

findings.summary: The page ships a custom `.modal`/WordPress editor overlay and no dialog, popover, or details primitives.
findings.evidence: The page ships a custom `.modal`/WordPress editor overlay and no dialog, popover, or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove leaked editor UI and use native dialog/popover primitives for any required overlay.

findings.summary: On mobile, logo, search, menu, eight category pills, and a domain banner consume roughly the first half viewport before content.
findings.evidence: On mobile, logo, search, menu, eight category pills, and a domain banner consume roughly the first half viewport before content.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary categories and domain messaging so primary content appears earlier.

findings.summary: Components resize at the viewport level, but CSS inspection found no container queries for reusable cards/navigation.
findings.evidence: Components resize at the viewport level, but CSS inspection found no container queries for reusable cards/navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Make card and navigation components adapt with container queries rather than only viewport rules.

findings.summary: Programmatic keyboard focus showed `outline: none`
findings.evidence: Programmatic keyboard focus showed `outline: none`; many controls are 34–43px high, below a 44px touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong `:focus-visible` ring and enlarge interactive targets to at least 44px.

findings.summary: The primary download journey diverts through multiple identical generic links to `linksmod.top`, rather than exposing a clear predictable file action.
findings.evidence: The primary download journey diverts through multiple identical generic links to `linksmod.top`, rather than exposing a clear predictable file action.
findings.suggestedFix: Present verified format/size actions directly, identify destinations, and remove avoidable link-shortener detours.

findings.summary: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8s and FCP 3.0s, outside the good loading range
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 3.8s and FCP 3.0s, outside the good loading range; CLS 0.042 and TBT 0ms were good.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset and remove load-chain overhead to bring LCP below 2.5s.

findings.summary: The load transferred 2.23MB across 83 requests
findings.evidence: The load transferred 2.23MB across 83 requests; four parser-inserted head scripts lack async/defer and the HAR found multiple blocking candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, remove redirects, and prioritize only resources needed for first content.

findings.summary: The public page ships WordPress admin editor, TinyMCE, media-upload, jQuery UI, and link-editor bundles unrelated to viewing movie listings.
findings.evidence: The public page ships WordPress admin editor, TinyMCE, media-upload, jQuery UI, and link-editor bundles unrelated to viewing movie listings.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop enqueueing admin/editor bundles and load page-specific scripts conditionally.

findings.summary: axe found a critical unnamed search button and a serious unnamed back-to-top link
findings.evidence: axe found a critical unnamed search button and a serious unnamed back-to-top link; search input also has no explicit label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon-only controls accessible names and explicitly label search fields.

findings.summary: axe measured ratios as low as 2.37:1 for search text and 3.03:1 for Telegram text, below 4.5:1.
findings.evidence: axe measured ratios as low as 2.37:1 for search text and 3.03:1 for Telegram text, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use WCAG AA color pairs for text, placeholders, controls, and notices.

findings.summary: axe found no main landmark and non-unique navigation landmarks
findings.evidence: axe found no main landmark and non-unique navigation landmarks; focus probing found no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap core content in `<main>`, uniquely name navigation landmarks, and restore visible focus.

findings.summary: Detail body copy renders low-contrast gray on charcoal with dense line breaks and inconsistent emphasis, reducing reading comfort.
findings.evidence: Detail body copy renders low-contrast gray on charcoal with dense line breaks and inconsistent emphasis, reducing reading comfort.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase body contrast, line-height, and spacing; use semantic headings instead of inline visual emphasis.

findings.summary: Narrow reflow works, but many category and navigation controls are only 34–43px high
findings.evidence: Narrow reflow works, but many category and navigation controls are only 34–43px high; the embedded trailer has no local text equivalent.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target sizes and provide captions/transcript or a clear equivalent for embedded media.

findings.summary: Lighthouse captured a TypeError in `width.js` reading `clientWidth` from null.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a TypeError in `width.js` reading `clientWidth` from null.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard missing elements in the plugin script or stop loading it on templates where its target is absent.

findings.summary: All 24 images use legacy PNG/JPEG without srcset
findings.evidence: All 24 images use legacy PNG/JPEG without srcset; 23 are oversized and the logo lacks dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit dimensions, responsive `srcset`/`sizes`, and modern image formats.

findings.summary: Public pages expose WordPress editor/link UI, load dated editor/plugin bundles, and create an iframe with an invalid `https://undefined/…` origin.
findings.evidence: Public pages expose WordPress editor/link UI, load dated editor/plugin bundles, and create an iframe with an invalid `https://undefined/…` origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove admin/editor assets from public templates and fix or remove the malformed iframe integration.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy headers are all absent.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy headers are all absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy headers.

findings.summary: The page contacted 15 third-party origins including analytics and opaque ad-like domains
findings.evidence: The page contacted 15 third-party origins including analytics and opaque ad-like domains; 79/83 HAR requests were classified third-party from the original host.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove opaque advertising chains, minimize analytics, and allowlist only necessary third parties.

findings.summary: No HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP/Trusted Types baseline is configured.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP/Trusted Types baseline is configured.
findings.suggestedFix: Add browser-enforced defensive policies, starting with HSTS and a nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: Runtime robustness is undermined by a null `clientWidth` exception and a malformed `https://undefined/…` iframe on the detail template.
findings.evidence: Runtime robustness is undermined by a null `clientWidth` exception and a malformed `https://undefined/…` iframe on the detail template.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally initialize plugins only when their target exists and validate all generated iframe origins.

findings.summary: `lang=en-US` is present, but CSS uses physical left/right properties and no logical inline/block properties despite multilingual content.
findings.evidence: `lang=en-US` is present, but CSS uses physical left/right properties and no logical inline/block properties despite multilingual content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical properties and set `dir` where content or localization requires it.

findings.summary: Primary “Download Links” are indistinguishable generic actions routed to an unrelated link-shortener while opaque ad scripts and an invalid hidden iframe load.
findings.evidence: Primary “Download Links” are indistinguishable generic actions routed to an unrelated link-shortener while opaque ad scripts and an invalid hidden iframe load.
findings.suggestedFix: Use honest destination labels, remove disguised advertising/redirect chains, and disclose any external host before navigation.

findings.summary: Comment fields rely on placeholder text, omit required semantics, and expose no evidence of interaction-timed or accessible validation.
findings.evidence: Comment fields rely on placeholder text, omit required semantics, and expose no evidence of interaction-timed or accessible validation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels, required attributes, `:user-invalid`, and announced error summaries after submission.

findings.summary: Name, email, URL, and search fields omit useful autocomplete tokens
findings.evidence: Name, email, URL, and search fields omit useful autocomplete tokens; search explicitly disables autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate autocomplete tokens such as name, email, and url; do not disable assistance without cause.

findings.summary: 23/24 images are oversized, all lack responsive sources, all use legacy formats, and 19 below-fold images load eagerly.
findings.evidence: 23/24 images are oversized, all lack responsive sources, all use legacy formats, and 19 below-fold images load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants and lazy-load below-fold posters.

findings.summary: The page loads 31 scripts including WordPress admin/editor stacks and unrelated UI libraries on a read-only listing.
findings.evidence: The page loads 31 scripts including WordPress admin/editor stacks and unrelated UI libraries on a read-only listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove non-user-facing bundles and conditionally load remaining features only when used.

findings.summary: Third parties account for about 2.23MB and 79 requests, including analytics, ad-like domains, fonts, and 1.47MB of images.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for about 2.23MB and 79 requests, including analytics, ad-like domains, fonts, and 1.47MB of images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, self-host essentials, remove opaque scripts, and defer non-critical media.
